assessment.headline: DAY 52, 7 AM MON: IRAN REJECTED TALKS. IRGC REBUILDING WEAPONS. USS SEIZED TOUSKA. ZERO Hormuz Sunday. Brent +5.8%. INDIA MARKETS OPEN IN 2 HOURS. Ceasefire expires TOMORROW. Most dangerous day since Feb 28.
assessment.body:
7 AM Monday April 20. India markets open in 2 hours. This is the situation.

IRAN OFFICIALLY REJECTED SECOND ROUND TALKS
• IRNA Sunday: absence stems from "Washington excessive demands, unrealistic expectations, constant shifts, repeated contradictions, and ongoing naval blockade"
• Supreme National Security Council: US proposals "still under review," further talks require US to "abandon excessive demands"
• Vance, Witkoff, Kushner flying to Islamabad — but Iran is not sending a delegation
• Without Iran attending, talks cannot happen
• This is the most definitive rejection since Islamabad round 1 collapsed April 12

IRAN IS REBUILDING ITS WEAPONS DURING THE CEASEFIRE
• IRGC Aerospace commander confirmed to IRIB state media: "Our speed in updating and refilling missile and drone launch platforms is EVEN GREATER than before the war"
• Iran has been rearming throughout the ceasefire (April 8-22)
• If ceasefire lapses tomorrow, Iran will have MORE strike capacity than it started with
• For India: Gulf oil infrastructure, tankers, and Indian vessels are all in range

USS SPRUANCE SEIZED TOUSKA — FIRST NAVAL BOARDING
• CENTCOM published video. 6-hour warning. Engine room fired on. Marines boarded.
• Iran vowed "swift response" from armed forces
• First Iranian ship physically seized since war began
• 25 ships total turned back under US blockade

ZERO HORMUZ TRANSIT SUNDAY
• CNN from ship tracking: zero tankers — quietest day since war began
• Brent +5.8% to $95.64 on Sunday open
• Iran turned back two more tankers Sunday
• IRGC targeting order on all approaching vessels remains active

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR INDIA — NEXT 2 HOURS
• Sensex at 78,494 (last close April 17)
• Brent at $95.64 — petrol/diesel hike risk, LPG cut fully reversed
• Rupee heading toward 94.20-94.50
• India VIX to open at 25-28 — near war-peak
• Multiple Indian-flag vessels attacked, MEA summoned Iran ambassador
• Ceasefire expires TOMORROW — this opens a 9:15 AM-3:30 PM IST window of maximum uncertainty
• Infosys results Wednesday April 23 — next domestic anchor

SCENARIO PROBABILITIES (7 AM IST ASSESSMENT)
• Scenario A (30%): Iran somehow reverses rejection, talks happen Tuesday/Wednesday, ceasefire extended → Sensex opens 74,000-77,000
• Scenario B (50%): Ceasefire lapses April 22, Iran responds to Touska, strikes resume → Sensex gap-down 70,000-73,000, Brent $108-120, rupee to 96+
• Scenario C (20%): Both sides ignore expiry, de-facto standoff without new strikes → Sensex 73,000-76,000, Brent $97-102

VERDICT: India is heading into its most dangerous market open since February 28. Three simultaneous risks are materialising simultaneously: (1) Iran officially rejecting talks while ceasefire expires in 36 hours, (2) IRGC openly rearming during ceasefire, (3) US physically seizing Iranian ship — all while zero oil is moving through Hormuz and Brent is rising. The window for avoiding renewed conflict is narrowing by the hour.
